rationale: The buyer is identifiable — CTOs and engineering managers at 20–500-person SMBs — and the pain (engineering time wasted evaluating unvalidated AI-generated prototypes) is real and recurring. However, there is no hard willingness-to-pay evidence: the problem is more of an organisational process irritant than a line-item budget pain, so willingness to pay a SaaS fee is speculative. The product could be partially automated (a structured validation scorecard/form + async Claude analysis delivered by email), but the core value delivery likely involves human judgment or consulting framing, which constrains operational autonomy below the build gate floor of 7.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a 'Vibe Code Validator' — a lightweight form where a CEO or exec submits their AI-generated idea, and Claude produces a structured validation report (market size, buyer clarity, build cost proxy, top 3 objections) delivered to the engineering manager within minutes. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt chain + a Tally/Typeform intake form + a Stripe payment link ($49–$99 per report) hosted on a simple landing page — no coding by Youval. Outreach targets engineering managers and CTOs via LinkedIn and HN communities, framing it as 'a polite way to filter exec ideas before they hit the sprint board' — outreach batches go out only after Youval approves. Delivery is fully automated: Claude generates the report on form submission and emails it via SendGrid; billing is handled by Stripe. The only recurring human step is approving outreach batches. However, this is a hard sell without clearer WTP evidence — validate with 5 cold LinkedIn DMs offering a free first report before committing to build.
notes: operational_autonomy scored 5 — the service can be largely automated, but the value proposition edges toward consulting/advisory, and buyers may expect human-crafted analysis. Build gate for operational_autonomy (min 7) is not met, capping stage at validate. Recommend testing price sensitivity and async-only delivery acceptance before building.
